_readme: One entry per language being learned (same keys as docs/config.js). The scripts read this file to know which YouTube subtitles to look for and how to brief the AI teacher. Edit 'learner' to describe YOUR learners: it changes which phrases the AI picks and how it explains them.

zh.name: Mandarin Chinese
zh.learner: English-speaking children (about 6 to 14) growing up abroad, who hear a little Mandarin from family. Beginner to lower-intermediate.
zh.phrase_rule: A phrase is 1 to 6 Chinese characters. Write all Chinese in Simplified characters.
zh.pron_rule: Hanyu Pinyin with tone marks for the phrase (e.g. nǐ hǎo)
zh.example_pron_rule: Hanyu Pinyin with tone marks for the example sentence
zh.level_rule: the HSK level of the language in the video, written like 'HSK 2' (HSK 1 to HSK 6)
zh.extra_rule: Keep examples short (under 14 characters), with easy words a child would say.
zh.words_brief: common, concrete Mandarin words and short phrases a child can use every day (HSK 1 to HSK 3 level), in Simplified characters

vi.name: Vietnamese
vi.learner: An English-speaking adult beginner who works with Vietnamese colleagues and wants to chat with them, order food and travel in Vietnam.
vi.phrase_rule: A phrase is 1 to 5 words, written with all Vietnamese accent marks.
vi.pron_rule: an easy English-style respelling a beginner can read aloud (e.g. 'sin chow' for 'xin chào'), following the accent heard in the video
vi.level_rule: the level of the language in the video: A1, A2, B1 or B2
vi.extra_rule: Keep examples short and practical: things said at work, in a cafe, at a market or with friends.
vi.words_brief: common Vietnamese words and short phrases an adult beginner needs for greetings, food, coffee, the office, getting around and friendly small talk
word_topics: family words and how to address people
